name: Guangzhou Library
features: Stacked, cascading 'book' forms on the facade; the design concept is 'Beautiful Books'.
note: Wikipedia: new building opened 23 June 2013. Most other category photos are night shots, so only the daylight one is listed; it shows the main block but crops the right-hand wing.

name: Capital Museum
features: Stone-clad exterior wall meant to symbolise the city walls and towers of ancient China.
note: Wikipedia says the museum moved into its present building in 2006 (no separate completion date). A small bus and car sit in the foreground of the first photo.

name: Beijing Television Cultural Center (TVCC)
features: A continuous lobby gives access to a 1,500-seat theatre and public facilities under one folded volume.
note: Opened 16 May 2012 after a 2009 fire (infobox gives 2009). Check the TVCC isn't already on the wall under another name (taken.txt has CCTV only). The first photo is a tall portrait crop; the second has part of CCTV Headquarters on the right.

name: Wuhan Railway Station
by: AREP, Fourth Survey and Design Institute of China, MaP3, SNCF-IGOA
features: Nine separate parts stand for China's nine provinces; the roof takes its form from the yellow crane, Wuhan's symbol.

photos.file: File:20240621 West facade of Wuhan Railway Station.jpg

note: Won a two-phase competition in 2005; built 2006 to December 2009. The first photo is a wide panorama (3573x1588); the second has two small figures on the forecourt.

name: Tainan Art Museum
by: Sutejiro Umezawa; Shi Zhao Yong and Shigeru Ban
features: Ochre-tiled Art Deco building of 1930 beside a new wing shaped after Delonix regia, the royal poinciana.

photos.file: File:Tainan Art Museum Building 1 (台南市美術館1館）.jpg

note: Building 1 was the 1930 Tainan Police Department; the museum opened 27 January 2019. Only building 1 has a photo in the category listing I saw; building 2 (Ban) photos should be looked for in a sub-category.

name: Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre
features: Glass curtain wall, the world's largest when built, looking over Victoria Harbour on three sides.
note: Old wing 1988, Topside 1989, New Wing 1994-97 (Wikipedia). Photo is from across the harbour, daylight; a Philips sign sits on a neighbouring tower behind it.

name: Hong Kong Central Library
features: Plan built from three shapes: the circle for sky, the square for land, the triangle for accumulated knowledge.
note: Opened 17 May 2001; Wikipedia names Ho Chiu-fan, a government senior architect, with Rocco Yim's alternative design not chosen. Photo is the front facade in daylight, trees in the lower part.

name: Shanghai Astronomy Museum
features: No straight lines or right angles; the forms express some of the fundamental laws of astrophysics.
note: Opened 2021 in Lingang. The second photo has the museum's name sign in the grass in front.

name: Run Run Shaw Creative Media Centre
features: Daniel Libeskind's building for City University of Hong Kong's creative media school, designed with Leigh & Orange.

photos.file: File:Run Run Shaw Creative Media Centre.JPG

note: Opened October 2011 in Kowloon Tong; Wikipedia says the design received several awards. Wikipedia gives few design details, so the features line is modest.

name: Shekou Cruise Center
features: Triangular terminal with 12 ferry berths and 2 cruise-ship berths.
note: Wikipedia: construction began 2014, new terminal due to open 1 November 2016. Photo shows the terminal from the water with two ferries in front.

name: Marisfrolg Pavilion
features: Biomimetic forms drawn from tropical plants and insect exoskeletons, clad in a mosaic of tile, brick and stone.
note: Construction began 2008; Wikipedia gives 2023. The photo shows the entrance side with the winged canopy rather than the whole complex, so the reviewer should confirm it works as a wall tile.

name: New Beijing Poly Plaza
features: Glass cable-net wall, called the world's largest; the lantern atrium has no support columns at the ground.
note: Office tower, counted as one of the 'ordinary' types; reason is the record-size cable-net wall (Wikipedia).

name: The Bund Finance Center
features: Three layers of gold stainless-steel tubes, inspired by Chinese theatre curtains, rotate slowly around the building.

photos.file: File:The Bund Finance Center in Shanghai.jpg

note: Wikipedia credits Foster + Partners with the design and Heatherwick as creative director; infobox year 2017. Rated 'quality' on Commons. A white car is on the road at the base of the first photo.

name: HSBC Building, the Bund
features: Main trading hall has columns made from whole marble blocks, unusual in Asia at the time.
note: Built 1921-23. Counted as an 'ordinary' type (bank HQ) but a historic Bund landmark. Wikipedia's marble-columns line says unusual in Asia at the time.

name: Wukang Mansion
features: French Renaissance style; the oldest veranda-style apartment building in Shanghai.
note: Counted as housing (ordinary type) but a named landmark by Hudec. Street traffic and pedestrians are small in the first photo.

name: Custom House, Shanghai
features: Four Doric columns mark the main entrance; the eastern section is eight storeys facing the Huangpu River.
note: Completed 19 December 1927. The first photo is a close upward view of the facade; the second shows it in the Bund row with a few small figures.

name: Phoenix Center
features: Sculptural shape from a Mobius strip, modelled in Digital Project; it resembles a looped DNA double helix.
note: no main photo. Candidates seen: 'Phoenix Center, Beijing 2.jpg' (CC0, clean dome end but only part of the building), 'Phoenix Center, Beijing 1.jpg' (CC0, PHOENIX sign in front), 'Phoenix Center (20241010161748).jpg' (sign and a person). Wikipedia names Shao Weiping as executive chief architect for BIAD.

name: National Speed Skating Oval
by: Populous, Beijing Institute of Architectural Design
features: Facade of 22 'ice ribbons', each 622 m long, around the 2022 Winter Olympics speed-skating hall.
note: no main photo. The only file in the category I could see is a rink interior; Wikipedia's lead image is not yet looked at. Needs a ground-level daylight exterior.

name: UCCA Center for Contemporary Art
features: Former East German factory in the 798 Art District, renovated in 2007; the spaces keep traces of their industrial past.
note: no main photo. The two category photos are a close view with banners and the red UCCA letters at the entrance. Original factory designed by Dessau Design Institute architects (Wikipedia).

name: Hangzhou Olympic Sports Expo Center
features: Exterior drawn from silk texture and the Qiantang River: 28 large and 27 small petal-like steel forms.
note: Main stadium. The photo is daylight with a wide empty plaza and some stacked barriers in front; the stadium fills about half the width, so the reviewer should judge if it is big enough for a tile. Two other photos had crowds and were left out.

name: Taichung Main Public Library
features: Seismic-isolated steel frame, seven floors above ground and two below, by Kazuyo Sejima and Ryue Nishizawa.

photos.file: File:Taichung Main Public Library (Taichung Green Museumbrary) 2025-11-05.jpg
File:Taichung Main Public Library (Taichung Green Museumbrary) 2025-11-05 (2).jpg

note: Wikipedia says the new building began trial operation on 28 October 2025, so the year is the opening year. Check the wall doesn't already hold it under 'Taichung Green Museumbrary'.

name: Kaohsiung Main Public Library
by: Ricky Liu, with Toyo Ito's team
features: Called the world's first column-suspended green building: no interior columns and a subtropical rooftop garden.
note: Opened to the public November 2014; Phase II tower 2020 (Wikipedia). Wikipedia names 'Ricky Liu and the team of Japanese architect Toyo Ito'. The second photo has a few people at the base.

name: Rockbund Art Museum
features: Chipperfield's restoration kept the original 1932 street facade and a minimalist approach.
note: Original building 1932-33; Wikipedia gives Chipperfield's restoration as beginning in 2007 and no completion date for it. Photo is a tall daylight view of the whole facade.

name: Digital Beijing Building
features: Solid and void alternate like 0 and 1; the ends suggest a barcode, the long faces a circuit board.
note: Opened 3 November 2007. Photo taken through a car window; a few cars at the right edge. Another photo had a red bus in front and was left out.

name: Beijing National Indoor Stadium
by: Glöckner³ with Beijing Institute of Architectural Design
features: Form likened to a traditional Chinese folding fan, hence the nickname 'the Fan'.
note: Opened 26 November 2007. Wikipedia credits Glöckner³ (won the Oct 2003 competition) with BIAD; its infobox lists two Beijing institutes. Rated 'valued' on Commons. Photo is an elevated daylight view in light haze.

name: Chung Tai Chan Monastery
features: A 136 m tall mountain monastery in a deliberately modern idiom, among the tallest and largest in the world.

photos.file: File:Remote view of the Chung Tai Chan Monastery 20190811.jpg
File:台湾 中台禅寺 - panoramio (1).jpg

note: Wikipedia: 'widely admired as an architectural masterpiece' for its more modern look. The lead photo is a hazy view from a distance; the second shows only the main tower behind trees.

name: Tianjin Grand Theatre
by: Gerkan, Marg and Partners (gmp), East China Architectural Design & Research Institute
features: Round theatre raised above a man-made lake; the round shape refers to the concept of heaven.
note: Completed and opened 22 April 2012. Rated 'quality' on Commons. One small person with an umbrella sits at the lakeside in the foreground.

name: Taipei Guest House
by: Dōgo Fukuda, Ichiro Nomura (rebuilt by Matsunosuke Moriyama, 1911)
features: Concave plan with a Mansard roof and tall Roman pillars, in the manner of French Second Empire palaces.
note: Completed 26 September 1901 (Wikipedia). The first photo is a view from above through the garden trees; the building is about 40 percent of the width.

name: Guangdong Museum
features: Inspired by the Cantonese ivory puzzle ball; the main circulation is a spiral stair from first to top floor.
note: New museum opened May 2010 (Wikipedia, Guangdong Museum). The architect is not named in that article's text; the Rocco Design Architects article lists it among the firm's works. Photo: clean daylight front with empty plaza.

name: Presidential Office Building
features: A 60 m central tower, once the tallest structure in the Taipei Basin; the east front faces Ketagalan Boulevard.
note: Built 1912 to 31 March 1919 (Wikipedia); Nagano's selected design, Moriyama's final design. The photo shows festive flag strings across the front; most other category photos have crowds, ceremonies or protests.

name: Fulfillment Amphitheater
features: Open performance space 40-51 m wide with 6,036 seats on three floors.
note: no main photo. Seen: 'Taichung Fulfillment Amphitheatre.JPG' (a large steel sculpture stands in front) and 'Wen-Hsin Forest Park ...' (far away). Opened 5 August 2006 (Wikipedia).

name: Court of Final Appeal Building
features: Two-storey neo-classical granite building on Ionic columns, topped by a blindfolded statue of Justice.
note: no main photo. Seen two daylight shots, but taxis and railings fill the foreground and towers crowd the background. Completed 15 January 1912 (Wikipedia).

name: Taipei Dome
features: Oval stadium beside the former Songshan Tobacco Factory (now Songshan Cultural and Creative Park).
note: no main photo. Seen: a gate view with a barrier and an aerial from Taipei 101. Wikipedia infobox says built 20 May 2023; opened October 2023.

name: Kai Tak Sports Park
features: Designed around a covered Kai Tak Sports Avenue; the main stadium has a retractable roof.
note: no main photo. The first photo seen is a pedestrian street between colourful facades with people. Wikipedia: opened 1 March 2025; body says completed 2024.

name: Beijing South Railway Station
features: Glass ceiling fitted with 3,246 solar panels over a sprawling ray-like form, built from over 60,000 tons of steel.
note: no main photo. Seen: a night view, and a daytime view with large red station signs and pedestrians. Opened 1 August 2008 (Wikipedia).

name: National Museum of China
by: Gerkan, Marg and Partners (2011 renovation); original 1959 architects not named
features: Front of ten square pillars, 313 m long; reopened in 2011 after a renovation by gmp.
note: no main photo. Seen: a wide shot with a crowd on Tiananmen Square and a close shot with a red banner. One of the Ten Great Buildings (1959).
